If <MATH_0005> is locally on <MATH_0006> generated by a Koszul-regular
(resp.<SPACE_0003><MATH_0007>-regular, quasi-regular) sequence in <MATH_0008>, then <MATH_0009>
is locally on <MATH_0010> generated by a Koszul-regular
(resp.<SPACE_0004><MATH_0011>-regular, quasi-regular) sequence in <MATH_0012>. This is
More on Algebra, Lemma <REF_0005>.

In this section we find some properties of morphisms of schemes
for which we could not (yet) show they are local on the base in
the fpqc topology which, however, are local on the base
in the fppf topology.

<LOCKED_0001>

<LOCKED_0001>

is fppf local on the base.

<STRUCT_0001>
The property of being an immersion is stable under base change,
see Schemes, Lemma <REF_0001>.
The property of being an immersion is Zariski local on the base.
Finally, let
<MATH_0001> be a surjective morphism of affine schemes,
which is flat and locally of finite presentation.
Note that <MATH_0002> is open by
Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>.
Let <MATH_0003> be a morphism.
Assume that the base change <MATH_0004> is an immersion.
In particular we see that <MATH_0005> is locally closed.
Hence by Topology, Lemma <REF_0003>
we see that <MATH_0006>
is locally closed. Let <MATH_0007> be
the closed subset <MATH_0008>.
By Topology, Lemma <REF_0004>
again we see that <MATH_0009> is closed in <MATH_0010>.
Hence we may apply Lemma <REF_0005>
to the fpqc covering <MATH_0011>
and conclude that <MATH_0012> is a closed
immersion. In other words, <MATH_0013> is an immersion.
Therefore Lemma <REF_0006> applies and we win.
<STRUCT_0002>

<STRUCT_0001>
<LOCKED_0001>

is fppf local on the base.

<STRUCT_0001>
By Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0001>,
dominant morphisms are preserved
under pullback by open morphisms, hence
by flat morphisms locally of finite presentation
(Morphisms, Lemma <REF_0002>).
The other direction is easier.
Indeed, being dominant is clearly Zariski local on the base.
Next, let <MATH_0001> be a surjective morphism of schemes
(not necessarily flat or locally of finite
presentation),
and let <MATH_0002> be a morphism. Assume that the base change
<MATH_0003> is dominant. Then <MATH_0004> is a composition
of two dominant morphisms, hence dominant. Since this is also
the composition <MATH_0005>, it follows that <MATH_0006> is dominant.
<STRUCT_0002>
